The trap design is composed of three concentric planar ring electrodes with outer radii of 126 μm, 600 μm, and 1100 μm.
The trap potential has a minimum at a radius of ~58 μm, a height of 385 μm, and a trap depth of 0.134 eV.
The single-ion trap frequencies are 1.03 MHz in the radial direction and 1.02 MHz in the vertical direction.
Molecular dynamics simulations show that a ring crystal of up to 92 ions can be formed with the given trap parameters.
Adding one more ion to the 92-ion ring results in a two-layer structure with a ~1 μm separation between the layers.
The energy barrier caused by a homogeneous electric field can be drastically reduced by increasing the number of ions in the ring.
A 10 μm × 10 μm square electrode with a voltage difference of up to 50 V can create an electric field of 100 V/m at the center of the ion ring.
For a 25-ion ring, the energy barrier caused by the square electrode imperfection is already sufficiently small.
The maximum torque from the radiation pressure of a displaced laser beam can be counteracted by applying a 75 V/m homogeneous electric field.
The equilibrium rotation frequency of the 30-ion ring is approximately 1.04 kHz per 1 μm displacement of the cooling laser beam.
